questions.sub_skill: Manage access to storage, including access policies
questions.prompt: A contractor holds a SAS URL for a container, issued a year ago with no stored access policy. Their engagement ended six months ago and the URL still works. How can you revoke it?
options: Delete the stored access policy it references
Remove the contractor's Entra account
Rotate the storage account key it was signed with
Set the account's SAS expiration policy to one day
questions.explanation: A SAS with no stored access policy carries its permissions inside the signed token, so the only way to kill it early is to rotate the account key - which breaks every other consumer simultaneously. It has no Entra identity to remove, and the SAS expiration policy is a recommendation surface, not enforcement. This is the most common real finding in a storage review.

questions.sub_skill: Implement and configure security for storage accounts
questions.prompt: You set AllowSharedKeyAccess to false on a storage account. Which credentials stop working?
options: The account keys
An account SAS
A service SAS
A user delegation SAS
questions.explanation: Account SAS and service SAS are both signed with the account key, so disabling shared key kills them along with direct key use. A user delegation SAS is signed with a key Entra issues on behalf of a principal and survives. One switch collapses four authorization systems to two, and closes the listKeys path that makes Contributor a data-plane role.

questions.prompt: A storage account has its firewall set to Deny with one virtual network rule. A VM in that subnet, holding no role assignment and no key, receives 403. Is the firewall working correctly?
options: No - the VNet rule should have granted the VM access
Yes - network rules subtract, they never grant; the request still needs an authorization system
No - VNet rules require the service endpoint plus a private endpoint
Yes - VNet rules apply only to the control plane
questions.explanation: Being on an allowed network does not authorize anything. The firewall decided the request was permitted to arrive; one of the four authorization systems still has to accept it. Reading an allowed network as an implicit grant is the standard misconception here.

questions.sub_skill: Implement Defender for Storage threat protection configurations
questions.prompt: Malware scanning is enabled with the default monthly cap on an account receiving 40 TB of uploads a month. What happens?
options: Scanning throttles, so every blob is scanned more slowly
The cap is raised automatically and billed at the standard rate
Scanning stops for the rest of the month once the cap is reached, and uploads are no longer scanned
Uploads are blocked once the cap is reached
questions.explanation: The default cap is 10,000 GB per storage account per month. When it is reached, uploads stop being scanned until the next month. Nothing about the storage account looks different, which makes it a detection gap you configured rather than one you were given.

questions.sub_skill: Manage access to storage, including access policies
questions.prompt: A requirement states that a shared access signature must be attributable to a named user and must not grant more than that user already has. Which type satisfies it?
options: Account SAS
Service SAS bound to a stored access policy
User delegation SAS
Any SAS, provided the account has Entra authorization enabled
questions.explanation: Only a user delegation SAS has a principal behind it. It is signed with a key Entra issues on that principal's behalf, cannot exceed their own RBAC, lives at most seven days, and is revocable by revoking the delegation key. It is Blob only.
